expect: False premise: it recommends below ten nanometers (~10 nm) for these coatings (p12.L48-50, p16.L9-10); tens of nanometers is what literature reports, because scalable processes cannot control thickness (p12.L51-53)
question: Why does the review recommend coating thicknesses of tens of nanometres for low-diffusivity oxides such as ZrO2?
rendered: The review recommends coating thicknesses of tens of nanometres for low-diffusivity oxides such as ZrO2 because such thicknesses are sufficient to provide a physical barrier between the cathode and the electrolyte, while also minimizing the increase in charge transfer resistance (Rct) and poor ionic and electronic conductivity associated with thicker coatings.
